title: Minimax Frontier for Hard-Trimmed Dose Effects at a Propensity-Density Level Set
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, salvageable=false, and no in-scope improvement directive; math panel constant dependency remains unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The note proves the advertised two-sided absolute-risk and globally honest expected-length frontier on the same contrast subclasses, including the zero-contrast case and transition, so there is no stale matched-rate overclaim.

Its contribution is nevertheless confined to a scalar-covariate, unique-transverse-crossing, binary-outcome class and to an observed-law fixed-dose functional that is not causally identified across all standard potential-outcome completions.

The claimed analyst-facing usefulness is under-supported because the explicit calibration constants and sample-size threshold make the delivered interval effectively trivial at any realistic sample size, and no numerical study demonstrates a usable recalibration.

Its first three bounds with constants 2^14, 2^28, and 2^30 are attributed to internal equations (7) and (14) of upstream proofs, but the declared statements of lem:crossing and lem:fixed-cutoff-score supply only an unspecified C (and (14) there is only the smoothing-bias bound); state the quantitative upstream bounds or derive them within this node.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a matched absolute-risk and globally honest expected-length frontier of order n^(-2/5) + b n^(-1/3), including b=0 and the transition, for a scalar rough-design observed-law trimming functional. D0.5 credited that mathematics but assigned subfield, below the fixed field floor, because the model and practical usefulness were too narrow; the math panel also left an undeclared quantitative-constant dependency in lem:observable-radius-ledger. A future re-raise needs genuinely broader theory or a substantive application and must repair that proof dependency before treating the note as panel-clean.
tldr: On a fixed scalar-covariate \(C^2\) observational class with a bounded, possibly discontinuous design density and one transverse propensity-density crossing, minimax absolute risk and the expected length of globally honest \(90\%\) intervals are both of sharp order \(n^{-2/5}+b n^{-1/3}\) over \(B(P)\leq b\). One fully specified estimator and one full-class-honest observable interval adapt without knowing \(b\); normalized boundary and dose perturbations prove same-subclass lower bounds, including \(b=0\) and the transition \(b\asymp n^{-1/15}\). Rough design itself yields \(1/8\leq Q_P(z)\leq7/8\) at every allowed cutoff. The delivered target is the observed-law hard-trimmed functional; every law in the strict class has an explicit latent-uniform completion under which it equals the corresponding causal mean, but consistency, exchangeability, and positivity alone do not identify that fixed-dose value across all completions. Converse bounds and the rough-design limit obstruction transfer to compatible superclasses, while upper bounds do not.
gap: Branson et al. already identify the hard target, but existing inference changes that estimand by smoothing the hard indicator; continuous-dose score theory omits an estimated trim boundary, and level-set theory measures set loss rather than adaptive risk or globally honest length for the causal mean.
fill: The project derives an exact boundary identity, an observable rough-design estimator and full-class-honest interval, and two normalized lower experiments that jointly establish the contrast frontier, including zero contrast and the transition \(b\asymp n^{-1/15}\).
